deep.reconstruction:
Setting: H is a Hilbert space and L^p(H) is the Schatten–von Neumann class, with L^∞ read as compact operators in operator norm. The question is when a sequence of hermitian H_i in L^p converges to H_0 in the L^p (quasi)norm.

Proposition. H_i → H_0 in L^p if and only if both of the following hold.
(1) ||H_i||_p → ||H_0||_p. It is enough to have limsup ||H_i||_p ≤ ||H_0||_p.
(2) A local spectral condition. For each λ in the spectrum of H_0 (tacitly λ ≠ 0), choose α > 0 so that:
- no other spectral value μ ≠ λ of H_0 satisfies |λ − μ| ≤ α;
- λ ± α lies in the spectrum of no H_i.
Let h_i be the spectral component of H_i in [λ−α, λ+α], i.e. H_i restricted to the range of the spectral projection. Then rank(h_i) is eventually equal to rank(h_0) = mult(λ), and h_i → h_0. The topology need not be specified, because the h_i live in a fixed finite-rank situation; this rests on a 'preliminary proposition' identifying the relevant topologies there.

Proof sketch (p < ∞).
- Necessity: L^p convergence implies operator-norm convergence. Riesz projections for the isolated eigenvalue λ then converge in norm, so ranks eventually agree and the compressed blocks converge.
- Sufficiency: cut out finitely many windows around the largest |λ|. On these finite-rank blocks we have convergence.
- On the complement, p-th powers of Schatten norms are additive over orthogonal spectral pieces. The limsup condition then forces the p-norm of the remainder of H_i to be eventually smaller than the tail of H_0 plus ε.

Corollary 1. For hermitian sequences, H_i → H_0 in L^p if and only if ||H_i||_p → ||H_0||_p and H_i → H_0 in L^∞ (operator norm). This is a Kadec–Klee / Radon–Riesz type property of Schatten classes relative to the operator-norm topology, valid also for p = 1.

Corollary 2. A ↦ |A|^r is continuous from L^p to L^{p/r}. Write it as a composite:
- A ↦ A*A, continuous L^p → L^{p/2} by Hölder;
- H ↦ H^{r/2} on positive elements of L^{p/2} → L^{p/r}.
The page breaks off here. The next page verifies the Proposition's hypotheses for the second map:
- condition 1 is trivial, since tr((H^{r/2})^{p/r}) = tr(H^{p/2});
- condition 2 reduces to finite-dimensional continuity of Σλ_i a_i⊗a_i ↦ Σλ_i^{r/2} a_i⊗a_i.
Since p/r may be < 1, quasi-Banach Schatten classes are implicitly allowed.

The neighbouring page goes on to ask:
- whether weak convergence plus norm convergence suffices (uniform convexity of L^p);
- whether ||H^r − K^r||^{1/r} is monotone in r, i.e. a Schatten-norm Hölder-type estimate for the operator power function.
errors: Condition 2 must exclude λ = 0. 0 belongs to the spectrum of any compact operator on infinite-dimensional H, is generally not isolated, and its spectral component is infinite-dimensional. The page does not say this.

The Proposition (and Corollary 1 under condition 1) is false for p = ∞. Take H_0 = diag(1,0,0,...) and H_i = H_0 + (1/2)·e_i⊗e_i. Then ||H_i||_∞ = ||H_0||_∞, and condition 2 holds since 1/2 is outside small windows around 1. Yet H_i does not converge in norm. The additivity of p-th powers used in sufficiency requires p < ∞. The '(resp. ...)' in Corollary 1 may be intended to handle this.
Requiring λ ± α to avoid the spectra of all H_i is stronger than needed; 'all but finitely many i' suffices. It is always achievable, since the union of countably many countable spectra is countable.
'Dimension' must be read as rank of the spectral projection, counted with multiplicity.

ideas.what: Characterization of Schatten-norm convergence of hermitian sequences: norm convergence plus convergence of finite-rank spectral blocks (eigenvalue clusters with multiplicities and eigenprojections)
ideas.modern_name: Kadec–Klee / Radon–Riesz property of Schatten classes; spectral (Riesz projection) perturbation theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Positive/states case: Dell'Antonio (1967), weak convergence plus trace norm implies trace-norm convergence. General S_1 and S_p results: Arazy (1981), Simon (Trace Ideals, 1979), Grümm (1973). For 1<p<∞, via uniform convexity: McCarthy (1967).
ideas.where_published: Not, to my knowledge, in the Memoir 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' or the Résumé; unsure

ideas.what: Corollary 1: for hermitians, L^p convergence ⇔ ||H_i||_p → ||H_0||_p and operator-norm convergence (including p = 1)
ideas.modern_name: Kadec–Klee property of S_p with respect to the operator-norm (or weak) topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Arazy 1981; Simon 1979; Dell'Antonio 1967 for density matrices

ideas.what: Corollary 2: continuity of A ↦ |A|^r from S_p to S_{p/r} (including quasi-normed range), via A ↦ A*A and the power map on positive operators
ideas.modern_name: Continuity of functional calculus / operator power maps in Schatten ideals; quantitative versions are Birman–Koplienko–Solomyak and Ando-type inequalities
ideas.usually_credited_to: Qualitative version largely folklore. Quantitative: Birman–Koplienko–Solomyak (1975), Ando (1988), Kittaneh–Kosaki (1987)

ideas.what: Use of Hölder for A ↦ A*A from S_p to S_{p/2}

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck proves a Kadec–Klee type theorem for hermitian elements of the Schatten classes, including the trace class. Norm convergence plus operator-norm convergence (equivalently, convergence of all nonzero eigenvalue clusters with eigenprojections) implies S_p convergence. This predates Dell'Antonio (1967), Grümm (1973), Simon (1979) and Arazy (1981).
missed.quote: Corollaire 1 Les deux conditions suivantes sont nécessaires et suffisantes pour la convergence de la suite H_i vers H_0 1) ||H_i||_p → ||H_0||_p (resp. ...) 2) H_i → H_0 dans L^∞(H)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority/historical point for operator ideal theory and quantum information, where trace-norm convergence of density matrices from weak convergence is standard. The result itself is now textbook, so there is no new mathematics.

missed.claim: The page sets up continuity of A ↦ |A|^r in S_p → S_{p/r}. The next page asks whether ||H^r − K^r||^{1/r} is monotone in r, i.e. ||H^r − K^r||_{p/r}^{1/r} ≤ ||H − K||_p for r < 1. That is essentially the Birman–Koplienko–Solomyak / Ando inequality, proved two decades later. The question was left open in these notes.
missed.quote: A → |A|^r est application continue de L^p dans L^{p/r}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Shows Grothendieck anticipated the quantitative operator-Hölder (operator-monotone power) estimates in Schatten norms, a precursor of the BKS/Ando/Aleksandrov–Peller line. Of historical, not mathematical, novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: These are clean, correct (modulo λ ≠ 0 and p < ∞) early versions of Kadec–Klee properties for Schatten classes, including the trace class, and continuity of power maps. Both were later published by others (1967–1988). They are now standard, so this is notable only as unrecorded priority.

The insertion above the struck '[λ−α, λ+α] ne contienne' appears to be 'n'existe': 'qu'il n'existe aucune valeur spectrale μ ≠ λ de H_0 telle que |λ−μ| ≤ α'.
The interlinear insertion above 'soit α>0 tel' reads approximately 'on écrit' (possibly 'on choisit'); uncertain.
The marginal '{+i→∞+}' belongs as the subscript of limsup: 'limsup_{i→∞} ||H_i||_p ≤ ||H_0||_p'.
